headline: Revenue and volumes grow, profit dips as FY guidance rises
summary_short: PayPal's Q2 2026 net revenue rose 5% y/y to $8.7 billion on 10% TPV growth, but GAAP net income fell 12% to $1.1 billion and diluted EPS dropped 3% to $1.25 as operating expenses outpaced revenue; PayPal raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance to roughly $5.38.
summary_long: Net revenues grew 5% y/y to $8.7 billion on 10% TPV growth, but GAAP operating income fell 5% to $1.4 billion and non-GAAP operating income fell 8% to $1.5 billion as opex growth (+7% y/y) outpaced revenue. GAAP net income fell 12% to $1.1 billion and diluted EPS fell 3% to $1.25, partly on a $0.07 negative swing from strategic-investment and crypto mark-to-market (vs a $0.01 gain a year ago). Cash and investments were $15.3 billion against $13.4 billion of debt; PayPal repurchased $1.5 billion of stock and declared a $0.14/share dividend. PayPal raised FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guidance to ~$5.38 and reaffirmed GAAP EPS guidance of a mid-single-digit decline.

drivers.explanation: CEO Enrique Lores cited stabilizing branded checkout, momentum in Venmo and Braintree, and diversification into financial services as the basis for raising full-year non-GAAP guidance despite near-term profit pressure.
Release attributes the 5% revenue increase to 10% TPV growth (9% FXN) and 8% growth in payment transactions.
TM$ grew a slower 1% than TM$ ex-interest-on-customer-balances (+3%), meaning lower interest earned on customer balances held back the headline figure.
